newsitem.title: USA: VTEL gets patent for video rate control.
newsitem.headline: VTEL gets patent for video rate control.

text.p: VTEL Corp said Monday it has been assigned a patent for the process and system for video rate control in a multipoint videoconference.
Patent number 5,594,725 was formally issued January 14, 1997, by the U.S. Patent & Trademark Office, VTEL said.
The process was invented by VTEL engineers Paul Tischler and Bill Clements, the company said.

"Participants in a multipoint videoconference have historically experienced bandwidth imbalance problems like loss of video synchronization, buffer overflow and the resulting video freezes and jerkiness," Tischler said in a statement released by the company. "VTEL and its customers both require the best quality video regardless of the number of participants in a videoconference. Our video rate control process makes that possible."

VTEL users in a multipoint videoconference are now able to exchange real data information such as in a PC conference, faxes and other point-to-point data channels without degrading the video and audio portion of the conference, the company said.
